With our latest patch, we’ve added a new in-game bug reporting tool and made several fixes to help leaderboards refresh faster and show your rank more reliably. Whether you have feedback to share or a high score to chase, Patch 1.2.2 brings a smoother experience to Dorfromantik.
We’ve added a new bug reporting tool directly to Dorfromantik. Just click the bug-shaped icon to open the form.

Since the latest patch, you can send us a message straight from the game and let us know whether you have encountered a serious issue or simply have some feedback for us. Once you submit the form, your report is sent directly to our development backend, where the team can review it more easily.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39260149/e7d4aec2e37354f1f4b55dcd4bad5de53a27c66c.png"]

Of course, you can still use the Steam Feedback sub-forum and our feedback channel on Discord. But when you spot something while playing and do not want to leave the game to report it, you now have a convenient in-game tool for that. 🙌

We have also made a few improvements to the in-game leaderboards. After their initial introduction, you discovered some reliability issues. Thank you again for your feedback on this. With the fixes in this update, leaderboard data should refresh faster and display your rank more consistently.
We hope you’re having a great (and hopefully bug-free) time!
You’ll find the full patch notes below.

releases.displayName: A Small Update on Big Wishes

items.text: We’re currently putting the final touches on a long-awaited community wish that will arrive this spring alongside our upcoming DLC. Since release, many of you have shared recurring ideas. We’re excited to finally bring one of those long-standing requests to life.

Since the release of Dorfromantik, there have been certain community wishes that keep coming up again and again. True evergreen topics. One of the biggest examples was the Undo Button, a feature many of you asked for from day one. We were happy to bring it into the game in 2022, and it’s been a core part of the experience ever since.
But of course, the Undo Button wasn’t the only idea.

notes.title: Community Wishes: So Many Wonderful Ideas

items.text: There are other requests that regularly find their way into our inboxes, comment sections, and forums. And while we genuinely love many of them at their core, we unfortunately can’t implement all of them.

Sometimes it’s the balancing of the base game that makes an idea difficult to realize. Sometimes it would require rebuilding large parts of Dorfromantik’s technical foundation from scratch. And sometimes, quite simply, it comes down to us being a small team.
To give you a bit of insight, some of the most requested additions that haven’t become reality include Mountains, Bridges for your train tracks, and a Night Mode.

notes.title: Here are just a few voices from the community

items.text: "Just like how we unlock the Windmill will there be possibilities to unlock more cool tiles? For example bridge that would allow rails to pass over water." - CrazyCory1230
"It should be 'jack of all trades' tile that fits all sides (it could be amusement park, zoo botanical garden or a mountain or something else)" - ostrowanet
"Little signposts to place, so we can name our towns, forests and lakes." - Spaz
"Ooooh. Yeah, night mode with lit houses etc sounds really neat." - The Renderer
"Make Pizza Hut special tile. It must be done." - Maf

We want you to know that we take these wishes very seriously. At regular intervals, we sit down as a team and review which ideas we might realistically bring to life, without compromising the heart of Dorfromantik. And this spring, we’re finally able to fulfill one long-standing community wish.

notes.title: The Surprise: Free for All Dorfromantik Players

items.text: For the surprise we’re preparing, we’re currently in the final stages of polishing. We’re refining the game feel and testing how the new addition integrates with the existing elements.
Timing-wise, we’ll reveal this surprise together with the upcoming DLC (read more about it here).

While the DLC will most probably be a paid one, the additional surprise will be free of charge for all Dorfromantik players. If you already have Dorfromantik in your Steam Library, you’ll receive the surprise simply by updating the game.

... and the catch? There isn’t one. We just felt that you’ve been waiting a long time for new content, and it wouldn’t feel right to release a paid DLC only. As passionate players ourselves, we always appreciate it when our favorite games surprise us with a few gifts every now and then. It's our way of saying: Thanks for sticking with us over all these years! 🎁

items.text: To celebrate the release of Dorfromantik for Nintendo Switch, the console update featuring the new Sakura Biome and full controller support is now also available for PC with this update.
🌸 New Sakura Biome
🎮 Full Controller Support
🚀 Performance Improvements
🌱 Additional Custom Mode Options

To celebrate the Nintendo Swtich release of Dorfromantik, we added a brand new cherry blossom biome featuring unique architecture and scenery to the game. Unlock the colorful biome by placing more than 2000 tiles in total to complete the Landscaper VI challenge.

The full controller support we implemented for the Nintendo Switch version is now also available to all PC players. The game is now also playable via the Steam Deck and should be marked as fully supported accordingly in the Steam Store in the next few days, as soon as the review on the part of Valve is completed.

In order to port Dorfromantik to the Nintendo Switch, we had to perform a lot of performance optimizations, which will now of course also benefit the PC version. We will fine-tune a few more parts so that we can meet the wide range of different hardware requirements for PC.

To neatly capture the gameplay for Nintendo Switch in smaller worlds due to technical reasons, we have introduced a new functionality called "world borders". Players can now create their landscapes within this area. This feature is now also available for everyone to use as a configuration option in Custom Mode.
For a more detailed overview of the new features and changes, feel free to check out the official patch notes:
We've been working with German board game publisher Pegasus for a while now to develop an analog Dorfromantik board game with the talented authors Lukas Zach and Michael Palm.
The game will be available as the German edition this December 2022 and will come out in English next year (2023).
Dorfromantik was recently released for Nintendo Switch and is available on the Nintendo eShop (more info on our website). Very soon it will also finally be verified for Steam Deck!
Now you can play Dorfromantik on the couch, on the train or wherever else you like!
No matter which platform you end up playing Dorfromantik on, we hope you enjoy your time playing.
Thank you for your support, as always! 💙💛

Last year we presented you our roadmap with the development plans for Dorfromantik during its Early Access period. Since then we have successfully completed and published all milestones, and are approaching the upcoming 1.0 release this spring.
We wanted to thank you for accompanying us through the last year. Now, what would be more appropriate than an additional update 0.5 with a little surprise?

For this update we have the biggest balancing changes for Dorfromantik yet, with which we want to improve the game experience in many areas for the classic game mode. Since we are using a RNG system to generate the tiles, we wanted to counteract some of the possible RNG frustration that can sometimes occur, through introducing various changes, such as adjusting the spawn probability of tiles and elements. You can find the detailed list of changes in our changelog.

A big thank you to all the dedicated testers in the beta program here in the Community Hub and on our Discord server who have helped us shape the game in a direction that keeps it as exciting to play for casual players as it is for all players who take a competitive approach.
As already announced, the new balancing will come into effect with this patch and the new leaderboard will be released to match the 1.0 release.

It's by far the most requested feature within the community and now it's finally here. We are very happy to give you this surprise as a big thank you for your help, cooperation and constructive feedback during the past months.

We have experimented with Dorfromantik on the Steam Deck and ported the basic controls for it. With this update you can play the classic mode of Dorfromantik with most features optimized for the Steam Deck. Full menu navigation, creative mode tools, quest edge highlighting as well as tutorial instructions are not yet implemented for Steam Deck and controller. You will however be able to use most of the functions via touch input.

In the future, all functionality will be fully supported for controller input, but we have decided to give you all access to the work in progress so that you can already play Dorfromantik on the Steam Deck. At the moment, we are focusing our full attention on the full release version and will dedicate ourselves to full Steam Deck and controller support after the launch this spring.
New Gamemode

We are currently working hard on the next update that we will release together with the full release 1.0. For this we will add another game mode, which will offer a wide variation of possibilities for how you can play Dorfromantik.
Price Change

With the start and during the Early Access phase we stated that we would like to thank all players who already put their trust in us with the current reduced price, and that the full version would come with a slight price increase. Since we would also like to put a nice launch discount on the new full price for the upcoming release, we have to increase the price at least 30 days before the actual release date. This is an official rule from Steam that we have to follow. As a result you can expect a price increase for Dorfromantik towards the end of March. You can also read more about the discount and price change rules from Valve themselves here.

In this patch we are trying a different approach to late game balancing. Instead of limiting the maximum number of quests and thus reducing the fun and motivation in the late game, we are now reducing the quest rewards when certain point count thresholds are reached. This change only affects scores above 50,000 and is intended to increase the difficulty when a point is reached where the rewards for perfect placement and quests can exceed the expense of placing tiles.

Based on very rough calculations, we suspect that infinite runs are still theoretically possible, but will be more difficult to achieve with the changes in 0.5.0.1. Feedback from those of you who have reached 100,000 or more points is again very important to us, as the main purpose of these changes is to maintain excitement in the very late game. If this fails, we will have to think about other alternatives.

The specific thresholds we have chosen to increase the difficulty are still up for debate. If this approach works, we will also ensure that the milestones achieved are presented in a more rewarding way than is currently the case (currently, UI crowns are displayed above the score after a threshold was reached).

We realize that for many of you, infinite runs where you have to create your own goals as a challenge (while the tile stack no longer offers any) are also a very enjoyable way of playing. With the upcoming Community Mode, planned for 1.0, we will include configurations that allow for such a play style. For classic mode, however, we want to make it very difficult or impossible for runs to last indefinitely.

Patch 0.5 will bring improvements to our general balancing. We have two main goals we want to achieve with these changes.

To improve the general experience, we increased probabilities of generally more useful tiles (e.g. lake variations or tiles with only one or two segments on them) and reduced the probabilities of very difficult or awkward to place tiles (e.g. tiles with many individual segments or tiles including the Y-shaped segment). Note that tiles are still chosen randomly, so all combinations (even very rare and unlikely ones) can appear.

notes.title: Preventing the game from getting easier

items.text: Our second goal is to make the difficulty level such that it is theoretically possible to play an infinite session without it getting easier at some point, which diminishes the value of progressing further. It is in the nature of perfect placements that a larger (perfectly built) world means a reduction in overall tile spending, as placement options increase and fewer tiles are needed to close edges.
However, we like the principle that a perfectly built world means the basic requirement for a theoretically ever-expanding game.

notes.title: That's why our balancing starts with the quests

items.text: Previously, a certain number of active quests on the map meant a reduced spawn rate of new quest tiles (about 1 in 20 tiles), but it remained at that level no matter how many quests there were. This resulted in maps in the late game having hundreds of quests active at a time and caused the stack to tend to increase instead of decrease after a certain point. Because of this, with this patch the probability of new quests continues to decrease until it reaches 0% when there are 15 active quests (not counting flag quests or preplaced tile quests).

So, in any case, from 0.5 onwards, it becomes more difficult to achieve extremely high scores. We have not yet been able to conclusively determine whether this solves the problem completely. Therefore, feedback from you would help us a lot, especially from the players who have already reached high scores of 100,000 points or more. We appreciate your feedback here in the Community Hub or in discussions on our Discord server.

items.text: Hi everybody,
The end of the year is just around the corner and we would like to give you a short overview of what you can expect for the winter holidays for Dorfromantik.
Finally we get to share it with you! Thanks to you, our wonderful community, we were nominated as one of 5 games for this year's Steam Awards in the Sit Back and Relax category.

We are very honored and of course we hope that we can win, so that we can finish a wonderful year of Dorfromantik together with you. You can help us by voting for Dorfromantik in the Sit Back and Relax category. Voting will be possible from next Wednesday December 22nd and throughout the Winter Sale continue.
Thank you already very much to everybody who takes the step to vote for us! We are very grateful 💛

We have completed a new content update for you to coincide with the Winter Sale and the voting period for the Steam Awards. Starting next week, you can expect our winter update if you want to play a relaxing session of Dorfromantik over the holidays.

What we can already reveal, there is definitely a new biome, which we may have already teased here somewhere ;) To hopefully get some uncertainties out of the way right away, as some questions came up regarding the previous content update for Halloween:
The Winter Biome will be unlocked for everyone directly in the game during the Winter Sale.
After that, it will still remain permanently in the game, but needs to be unlocked like all other biomes by completing the Landscaper challenge.
We'll share more information with you next week about the update with the start of the Winter Sale.

The Winter Sale will start next week Wednesday, December 22 and will last 2 weeks until January 5. During this time you can buy Dorfromantik and the soundtrack with 10% discount or give it to someone as a gift. We've also teamed up with our friends to put together games that we all love and think fit Dorfromantik very well into a wonderful Serene City Builder Bundle, which will be discounted combined.
While we will put out a proper Showcase announcement - We have heard you!

From now, until January 14th, we will be running a special Winter Edition Community Showcase! Build us a scene that makes us want to go walking in a winter wonderland, Go ham with the new Midwinter Biome, maybe sprinkle in a secondary one where appropriate.
Voting will start on January 10th, submissions as usual via Discord or, once we set it up, the Community Showcase Announcement comments.

Us six Toukans certainly will take some much needed and, hopefully, well-deserved time off, to recharge our batteries and creativity tanks. There is only one way to go after New Year's, after all, and that is the way towards Version 1.0!
Eat well, take plenty of naps, and enjoy. We've all earned it! 💛

Hey everyone,

Dorfromantik has been in Early Access for seven months already! A lot has happened, we brought in a Community Manager (Hi, I am writing this post!), brought you an all-new game mode in the Creative Mode and worked on a lot of Quality of Life features. As planned we move to the next chapter on our roadmap and bring you the first Content Update 0.3 for Halloween (see here for the full detailed patch notes):

We are adding a new biome, 'Enchanted', to the game. You will be able to unlock it permanently by completing the new Landscaper IV Challenge. During the Halloween event, it is unlocked for everyone by default, though! You might also be able to find pumpkins in your villages going forward.

We have heard you would like Lake Tiles that only occupy parts of a tile, opposed to the currently available water tile that is all water. These Water Tiles currently come in three new additional flavors:
3 Water Edges
4 Water Edges
5 Water Edges

We are thinking about adding a few more Water Tiles to the game in future updates. For example we already found a 2 Water Edge Tile would sometimes be highly appreciated to complete shorelines satisfyingly. Next to adding completely new Water Tiles, we also worked more fundamentally on the water shapes themselves and reworked them to get more diversity in their building structures.
Yup. We added more special tiles! Update 0.3 brings a total of six new special tiles including many new animals that will bring to life in your landscape:
Bears and cubs
Boars and their kids
Swans and geese
Beavers and their dams
Foxes and fox kits
Forest and water ruins
Try to unlock them all in Classic Mode and build fantastic vivid worlds in the Creative Mode.

Of course, new Special Tiles also bring new challenges! A total of 6 new challenges, one for every new Special Tile, are added to the game. On top we added a few more levels to already existing Challenges, which give you a total amount of 34 Achievements to unlock!
Planner - Score perfect placements at once.
Explorer - Connect preplaced tiles in total.
Flag Collector - Complete flag quests in total.
Heavy Weight - Place consecutive tiles without rotating a tile.
Quest Master - Complete quests in total.
Analyst - Collect points with a single tile placement.
That is not all, though! We have also added many other small features to improve the gameplay experience in Dorfromantik.

You can now adjust your various camera speeds - Scrolling, Zooming, Rotating - in the Keybinds Menu with ranges from 0.2x to 5x standard speed. We hope this makes traversing larger maps easier, or allows you to record those slow, cinematic shots of your creations!

We now have in-game statistics! these are on a save-by-save basis and include statistics like Playtime and Placed Tiles. These also work for older saves, so now you can finally find out how long you worked on those giant landscapes worth hundreds of thousands of points, and just how many Tiles you placed.

So, November and December will be a bit lighter on game updates. We have mentioned it a couple of times in the past, but the core team is diving into their Master Theses starting next week. They will still be working some hours on Dorfromantik every week, but obviously their priority will be fixing bugs and outside of that, smaller stuff.
We are also prioritizing Controller Support in the upcoming months, so you will be able to hopefully play Dorfromantik on the new Steam Deck by Valve as well as your common game controllers for PC.

We plan to bring you an additional Content Update just in time for Christmas to round off 2021 on a good note. Starting in 2022, as announced in our roadmap, we will work on a final third gamemode, as well as take another look at balancing to make the most polished game experience of Dorfromantik possible for you.

Big thank you to everybody who helped us out by providing their save-games as well as all the participants in our public beta program, all the data has helped us a lot already in identifying a bunch of points of attack and sparked a lot of internal discussions!

Lastly, our Community Manager has been locked away in his laboratory, tinkering with new ideas for Community Challenges, Showcases, and the like. Please look forward to those later this year. There might even be something for all the score-chasing Classic Mode players in there!

From all of us here at Toukana Interactive, we would like to thank you for your support over the last months, wish you a lot of fun with the new update and are excited to see what you create and hopefully share with us!! 💛💛💛
